prompt: Match each part of an agent to its job.

pairs.right: Decides which tool to call, or answers
Calls the tool, if allowed, and returns the result
Do the work: look up, read, refund

prompt: Where does the lesson put every limit an agent needs?
hint: The model cannot do anything a host does not do for it.

choices.text: In the system prompt, stated firmly
choices.why: A prompt is something the model continues from, not a rule it is bound by.

choices.text: In the model's training
choices.why: Training is not yours to change, and not a limit.

choices.text: In the host's code, below the model
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: In the provider's console
choices.why: The console sees requests, not your tools.

prompt: When the model asks for `issue_refund`, what has happened to the customer's money?

choices.text: Nothing yet
choices.why: Right: the host has not called anything.

choices.text: It has been refunded by the model
choices.why: A model runs nothing.

choices.text: It has been refunded by the provider
choices.why: The provider has no access to the shop.

choices.text: It is on hold at the payment service
choices.why: Nothing has reached the payment service.

prompt: How many steps did the agent take to answer about order 1042?
How does the host know the model has finished?
hint: Read the condition after the request.

choices.text: The model writes the word done
choices.why: Nothing parses words in the reply.

choices.text: `stop_reason` is not `tool_use`
choices.why: Right: no tool was asked for, so the reply is the answer.

choices.text: The step limit is reached
choices.why: That stops the loop without an answer.

choices.text: The tool results run out
choices.why: Results arrive only when tools are called.

prompt: Where did the 28 October in the answer come from?
hint: Two tool results and one step of reasoning.

choices.text: From the model's training
choices.why: The order is the shop's, and recent.

choices.text: From `get_order` alone
choices.why: That gave the delivery date, not the window.

choices.text: From the handbook alone
choices.why: That gave 30 days, not the date.

choices.text: Two tool results, added
choices.why: Right: the delivery date plus the 30-day window; each fact has a tool result behind it.

prompt: What does a model know about a tool it may call? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Its name
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Its description
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Its source code
choices.why: The model never sees the code.

choices.text: The schema of its arguments
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Why `get_order` and `issue_refund` rather than one `manage_order(action, ...)`?
hint: Which one could the host let run without asking?

choices.text: Fewer tools always cost fewer tokens
choices.why: One broad tool still needs a long description.

choices.text: MCP allows one argument per tool
choices.why: It allows any schema.

choices.text: Each one gets its own permission
choices.why: Right: the read can run, the refund can wait for a person.

choices.text: The model cannot call a tool with an action argument
choices.why: It can; that is not the reason.

prompt: Why does the description of `get_order` say "in cents"?
hint: Where else would the model learn it?

choices.text: Because the schema requires a unit
choices.why: Schemas have types, not units.

choices.text: Nowhere else says it
choices.why: Right: it is the only place the model learns the unit.

choices.text: To make the description longer
choices.why: Length is not the goal.

choices.text: Because MCP converts cents to dollars
choices.why: MCP passes values through unchanged.

prompt: MCP messages follow ___ 2.0: each request has an id, a method and params.
hint: Two words joined by a hyphen.

prompt: Put the by-hand MCP session in order.
Match each MCP role to what it is in this lesson.

pairs.right: The part of the host that talks to one server

right_distractors: The model, which runs the tools

prompt: Why does the section compare installing an MCP server to installing a program?
hint: Whose permissions does a stdio server run with?

choices.text: It runs on your machine, with your permissions
choices.why: Right: what it can reach, the model can ask for.

choices.text: Because servers must be compiled
choices.why: Python servers are not.

choices.text: Because MCP servers are sold in app stores
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Because the model installs it automatically
choices.why: A person installs it.

prompt: Where does the input schema of `get_order` come from?

choices.text: A JSON file next to the server
choices.why: There is no such file.

choices.text: The model writes it at the first call
choices.why: The server sends it in tools/list, before any call.

choices.text: The docstring
choices.why: The docstring becomes the description.

choices.text: The function's type hints
choices.why: Right: `order_id: str` becomes a required string.

prompt: Why raise `ToolError` rather than `ValueError` for a page outside the handbook?
hint: What reaches the client in each case?

choices.text: `ValueError` stops the server
choices.why: The server keeps running either way.

choices.text: Its message reaches the model
choices.why: Right: other exceptions send a generic one, which keeps a crash's details off the wire.

choices.text: `ToolError` is faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: `ValueError` is not allowed in Python 3.11
choices.why: It is.

prompt: A server you downloaded marks every tool `readOnlyHint=True`. What does that tell you?

choices.text: That every tool is safe to call without asking
choices.why: Only if you trust whoever wrote the server.

choices.text: Nothing; MCP ignores annotations
choices.why: Hosts read them; that is what they are for.

choices.text: What the server says about itself
choices.why: Right: a hint, trusted only as far as the server is.

choices.text: That the server cannot write files
choices.why: Nothing in the protocol stops it.

prompt: How many of the shop server's tools say they only read?
How does `read_handbook` refuse `../../.env`?
hint: It looks at where the path ends up.

choices.text: By where the path resolves to
choices.why: Right: it must be inside the handbook's folder.

choices.text: It refuses any name containing a dot
choices.why: `.md` is added by the tool; names have no dots anyway, but the check is on the resolved path.

choices.text: The schema forbids slashes
choices.why: The schema only says it is a string.

choices.text: The model is told not to ask for it
choices.why: Then a model that asks anyway gets the file.

prompt: After the operator answered `n`, what was in `data/refunds.log`?
hint: The `cat` after the first refund run.

choices.text: One refund of 7980 cents
choices.why: That is after the `y`.

choices.text: A refused entry
choices.why: Nothing was written.

choices.text: Two refunds
choices.why: There was only one yes.

choices.text: Nothing: the file did not exist
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Why does the approval prompt show the exact arguments?

choices.text: Because MCP requires it
choices.why: The host chose to show them.

choices.text: A summary is not the action
choices.why: Right: approving a summary is not approving what will happen.

choices.text: To make the log longer
choices.why: The log is separate.

choices.text: So the model can read them back
choices.why: The model already chose them.

prompt: Which are rules from the section? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Read-only tools by default
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Use the developer's own credentials, which already work
choices.why: The agent gets its own, scoped.

choices.text: Check arguments in the tool, not only in the schema
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Ask a person before anything that costs money
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Match each run to the guard that stopped it.
How many input tokens did the five steps of the wandering run add up to?
hint: The total in the last line.

prompt: Why did each of the five steps carry more input tokens than the one before?

choices.text: labllm charges more as the task goes on
choices.why: Prices do not change.

choices.text: The tool definitions grew
choices.why: They are the same three tools every step.

choices.text: History accumulates
choices.why: Right: each step carries every earlier call and result.

choices.text: The model's answers got longer
choices.why: There were no answers, only calls.

prompt: A team wants an agent that can cancel customers' orders. Which design follows from this lesson?

choices.text: A narrow cancel tool that checks the order, waits for a person's yes, inside a step limit
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A general database tool, with a prompt telling the model to only cancel
choices.why: A prompt is not a limit, and the tool can do anything.

choices.text: The developer's credentials, so the agent can do whatever the developer can
choices.why: The opposite of least privilege.

choices.text: No guards, since the model is a capable one
choices.why: Capability is not the issue; nothing in the loop checks it.
